items.title: Jack DeJohnette interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 7, 2025
items.q: Erykah Badu did an album called “Kiss Me on My Neck” and she sampled a track from my, what was it, “Sorcery” album.

ctx.x: How does it work in this business these days with — do you get payments for things you did over the years, or was it mostly you got a fee? I guess I’m talking about the many things you’ve done as a side person. Do you ever get checks in the mail and wonder what is this for?

Not from doing that. I mean you know I get fees that I suggest or demand that I get. You know you get a 1099 and do that. I mean there’s checks that would be like say Erykah Badu did an album called “Kiss Me on My Neck” and she sampled a track from my, what was it, “Sorcery” album. And she used it on two tracks but they never contacted my lawyer about the copyright of that. So as a result of that, a statutory rate, my lawyer got on there, paid us, paid Dave and I quite a sum over time you know.

Well it’s nice to know the system finally worked in that technology moves so quickly, do you think that composers and players these days write differently because of what’s possible in the recording studio with all the things you can do digitally and if someone’s a bit off it’s very fixable. I guess I’m just generally asking you how you feel about the state of technology in the music world?

items.title: Jack DeJohnette — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: which actually wound up being used on Erykah Badu’s “Kiss Me On My Neck”

ctx.x: I used that and played a little saxophone. Michael Fellerman who was a sculptor also played some trombone. We also did “Four Levels Of Joy,” some things with Dave Holland. Something called, “Epilogue,” which actually wound up being used on Erykah Badu’s “Kiss Me On My Neck” which is… that’s something else. But anyway, this was a fun record to do in my experimental years. It was fun doing that in that time, and recording at home of course was nice.
I have the LPs here. They were recorded in in March and May of 1974.
